passages.text: In the first year of Darius son of Xerxes, a Mede by descent, who was made ruler over the kingdom of the Chaldeans — in the first year of his reign, I, Daniel, understood from the sacred books, according to the word of the LORD to Jeremiah the prophet, that the desolation of Jerusalem would last seventy years.
passages.sermon:
Darius was the son of Xerxes.
Darius was a Mede by descent.
Darius became ruler over the kingdom of the Chaldeans.
This happened in the first year of Darius’s reign.
I am Daniel.
In that same first year, I studied the sacred books.
I read the word of the LORD given to Jeremiah the prophet.
I understood the number of years for Jerusalem’s desolation.
The LORD said Jerusalem would be desolate for seventy years.
passages.original: בִּשְׁנַ֣ת אַחַ֗ת לְדָרְיָ֛וֶשׁ בֶּן־ אֲחַשְׁוֵר֖וֹשׁ מִזֶּ֣רַע מָדָ֑י אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָמְלַ֔ךְ עַ֖ל מַלְכ֥וּת כַּשְׂדִּֽים׃ בִּשְׁנַ֤ת אַחַת֙ לְמָלְכ֔וֹ אֲנִי֙ דָּֽנִיֵּ֔אל בִּינֹ֖תִי בַּסְּפָרִ֑ים מִסְפַּ֣ר הַשָּׁנִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֤ה דְבַר־ יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ יִרְמִיָ֣ה הַנָּבִ֔יא לְמַלֹּ֛אות לְחָרְב֥וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם שִׁבְעִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה׃

passages.text: So I turned my attention to the Lord God to seek Him by prayer and petition, with fasting, sackcloth, and ashes.
passages.sermon:
Daniel was a prophet and a servant of God.
Daniel wanted to seek God.
Daniel turned his attention to the Lord God.
Daniel prayed to God.
Daniel asked God for help and mercy.
Daniel fasted.
Daniel wore sackcloth.
Daniel sat in ashes.
passages.original: וָאֶתְּנָ֣ה אֶת־ פָּנַ֗י אֶל־ אֲדֹנָי֙ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים לְבַקֵּ֥שׁ תְּפִלָּ֖ה וְתַחֲנוּנִ֑ים בְּצ֖וֹם וְשַׂ֥ק וָאֵֽפֶר׃

passages.text: And I prayed to the LORD my God and confessed, “O, Lord, the great and awesome God, who keeps His covenant of loving devotion to those who love Him and keep His commandments, we have sinned and done wrong. We have acted wickedly and rebelled. We have turned away from Your commandments and ordinances.
passages.sermon:
Daniel was a prophet of God.
\r\nDaniel prayed to the LORD his God.
\r\nDaniel confessed his sins to God.
\r\nDaniel said, "O Lord, You are great and awesome."
\r\nGod keeps His covenant.
\r\nGod shows loving devotion to those who love Him.
\r\nGod shows loving devotion to those who keep His commandments.
\r\nWe have sinned.
\r\nWe have done wrong.
\r\nWe have acted wickedly.
\r\nWe have rebelled.
\r\nWe have turned away from Your commandments.
\r\nWe have turned away from Your ordinances.
passages.original: וָֽאֶתְפַּֽלְלָ֛ה לַיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהַ֖י וָאֶתְוַדֶּ֑ה וָאֹֽמְרָ֗ה אָנָּ֤א אֲדֹנָי֙ הָאֵ֤ל הַגָּדוֹל֙ וְהַנּוֹרָ֔א שֹׁמֵ֤ר הַבְּרִית֙ וְֽהַחֶ֔סֶד לְאֹהֲבָ֖יו וּלְשֹׁמְרֵ֥י מִצְוֺתָֽיו׃ חָטָ֥אנוּ וְעָוִ֖ינוּ וְהִרְשַׁעְנוּ וּמָרָ֑דְנוּ וְס֥וֹר מִמִּצְוֺתֶ֖ךָ וּמִמִּשְׁפָּטֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: We have not listened to Your servants the prophets, who spoke in Your name to our kings, leaders, and fathers, and to all the people of the land.
passages.sermon:
We did not listen to Your servants.
Your servants are the prophets.
The prophets spoke in Your name.
They spoke to our kings.
They spoke to our leaders.
They spoke to our fathers.
They spoke to all the people of the land.
passages.original: וְלֹ֤א שָׁמַ֙עְנוּ֙ אֶל־ עֲבָדֶ֣יךָ הַנְּבִיאִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר דִּבְּרוּ֙ בְּשִׁמְךָ֔ אֶל־ מְלָכֵ֥ינוּ שָׂרֵ֖ינוּ וַאֲבֹתֵ֑ינוּ וְאֶ֖ל כָּל־ עַ֥ם הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: To You, O Lord, belongs righteousness, but this day we are covered with shame—the men of Judah, the people of Jerusalem, and all Israel near and far, in all the countries to which You have driven us because of our unfaithfulness to You.
passages.sermon:
The Lord is righteous.
We are covered with shame today.
The men of Judah are covered with shame.
The people of Jerusalem are covered with shame.
All Israel is covered with shame.
This includes those who are near.
This includes those who are far away.
We are in all the countries where You have scattered us.
You scattered us because we were unfaithful to You.
passages.original: לְךָ֤ אֲדֹנָי֙ הַצְּדָקָ֔ה וְלָ֛נוּ בֹּ֥שֶׁת הַפָּנִ֖ים כַּיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה לְאִ֤ישׁ יְהוּדָה֙ וּלְיוֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרֽוּשָׁלִַ֔ם וּֽלְכָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֞ל הַקְּרֹבִ֣ים וְהָרְחֹקִ֗ים בְּכָל־ הָֽאֲרָצוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִדַּחְתָּ֣ם שָׁ֔ם בְּמַעֲלָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר מָֽעֲלוּ־ בָֽךְ׃

passages.text: O LORD, we are covered with shame—our kings, our leaders, and our fathers—because we have sinned against You.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
We have sinned against God.
We feel shame because of our sin.
Our kings feel shame.
Our leaders feel shame.
Our fathers feel shame.
God, You see our shame.
passages.original: יְהוָ֗ה לָ֚נוּ בֹּ֣שֶׁת הַפָּנִ֔ים לִמְלָכֵ֥ינוּ לְשָׂרֵ֖ינוּ וְלַאֲבֹתֵ֑ינוּ אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָטָ֖אנוּ לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: To the Lord our God belong compassion and forgiveness, even though we have rebelled against Him and have not obeyed the voice of the LORD our God to walk in His laws, which He set before us through His servants the prophets.
passages.sermon:
The Lord is our God.
The Lord has compassion.
The Lord forgives.
We have rebelled against Him.
We did not obey the voice of the Lord our God.
We did not walk in His laws.
God gave these laws to us.
He gave them through His servants, the prophets.
passages.original: לַֽאדֹנָ֣י אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ הָרַחֲמִ֖ים וְהַסְּלִח֑וֹת כִּ֥י מָרַ֖דְנוּ בּֽוֹ׃ וְלֹ֣א שָׁמַ֔עְנוּ בְּק֖וֹל יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ לָלֶ֤כֶת בְּתֽוֹרֹתָיו֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתַ֣ן לְפָנֵ֔ינוּ בְּיַ֖ד עֲבָדָ֥יו הַנְּבִיאִֽים׃

passages.text: All Israel has transgressed Your law and turned away, refusing to obey Your voice; so the oath and the curse written in the Law of Moses the servant of God has been poured out on us, because we have sinned against You.
passages.sermon:
All Israel broke Your law.
All Israel turned away from You.
All Israel refused to obey Your voice.
You gave us an oath and a curse in the Law of Moses.
Moses was Your servant.
You poured out this oath and curse on us.
We sinned against You.
passages.original: וְכָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל עָֽבְרוּ֙ אֶת־ תּ֣וֹרָתֶ֔ךָ וְס֕וֹר לְבִלְתִּ֖י שְׁמ֣וֹעַ בְּקֹלֶ֑ךָ וַתִּתַּ֨ךְ עָלֵ֜ינוּ הָאָלָ֣ה וְהַשְּׁבֻעָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר כְּתוּבָה֙ בְּתוֹרַת֙ מֹשֶׁ֣ה עֶֽבֶד־ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים כִּ֥י חָטָ֖אנוּ לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: You have carried out the words spoken against us and against our rulers by bringing upon us a great disaster. For under all of heaven, nothing has ever been done like what has been done to Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
God spoke words against us.
God spoke words against our rulers.
God fulfilled these words.
God brought a great disaster upon us.
This disaster was very severe.
Nothing like this has happened anywhere under heaven.
Nothing like this has happened as it happened in Jerusalem.
passages.original: וַיָּ֜קֶם אֶת־ דְּבָרָיו אֲשֶׁר־ דִּבֶּ֣ר עָלֵ֗ינוּ וְעַ֤ל שֹֽׁפְטֵ֙ינוּ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שְׁפָט֔וּנוּ לְהָבִ֥יא עָלֵ֖ינוּ רָעָ֣ה גְדֹלָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־ נֶעֶשְׂתָ֗ה תַּ֚חַת כָּל־ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר נֶעֶשְׂתָ֖ה בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: Just as it is written in the Law of Moses, all this disaster has come upon us, yet we have not sought the favor of the LORD our God by turning from our iniquities and giving attention to Your truth.
passages.sermon:
The Law of Moses is God's instruction to Israel.
The Law of Moses warned about disaster for disobedience.
All this disaster has come upon us, just as the Law of Moses said.
We are Israel.
We have not sought the favor of the LORD our God.
We have not turned away from our sins.
We have not paid attention to God's truth.
passages.original: כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר כָּתוּב֙ בְּתוֹרַ֣ת מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֵ֛ת כָּל־ הָרָעָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את בָּ֣אָה עָלֵ֑ינוּ וְלֹֽא־ חִלִּ֜ינוּ אֶת־ פְּנֵ֣י׀ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ לָשׁוּב֙ מֵֽעֲוֺנֵ֔נוּ וּלְהַשְׂכִּ֖יל בַּאֲמִתֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: Therefore the LORD has kept the calamity in store and brought it upon us. For the LORD our God is righteous in all He does; yet we have not obeyed His voice.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is our God.
The LORD watched over the disaster.
The LORD brought the disaster upon us.
The LORD is righteous in everything He does.
We did not listen to His voice.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁקֹ֤ד יְהוָה֙ עַל־ הָ֣רָעָ֔ה וַיְבִיאֶ֖הָ עָלֵ֑ינוּ כִּֽי־ צַדִּ֞יק יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ עַל־ כָּל־ מַֽעֲשָׂיו֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וְלֹ֥א שָׁמַ֖עְנוּ בְּקֹלֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Now, O Lord our God, who brought Your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand, and who made for Yourself a name renowned to this day, we have sinned; we have acted wickedly.
passages.sermon:
O Lord, You are our God.
You brought Your people out of Egypt.
You used a mighty hand.
You made Your name great.
Your name is still known today.
We have sinned.
We have done wicked things.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֣ה׀ אֲדֹנָ֣י אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ אֲשֶׁר֩ הוֹצֵ֨אתָ אֶֽת־ עַמְּךָ֜ מֵאֶ֤רֶץ מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ בְּיָ֣ד חֲזָקָ֔ה וַתַּֽעַשׂ־ לְךָ֥ שֵׁ֖ם כַּיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה חָטָ֖אנוּ רָשָֽׁעְנוּ׃

passages.text: O Lord, in keeping with all Your righteous acts, I pray that Your anger and wrath may turn away from Your city Jerusalem, Your holy mountain; for because of our sins and the iniquities of our fathers, Jerusalem and Your people are a reproach to all around us.
passages.sermon:
The Lord is righteous in all His actions.
Jerusalem is God's city.
Jerusalem stands on God's holy mountain.
God, I ask You to turn away Your anger and wrath from Jerusalem.
I ask this because of Your righteousness.
We have sinned.
Our fathers have sinned.
Because of our sins and the sins of our fathers, Jerusalem is disgraced.
Your people are disgraced.
Everyone around us sees this shame.
passages.original: אֲדֹנָ֗י כְּכָל־ צִדְקֹתֶ֙ךָ֙ יָֽשָׁב־ נָ֤א אַפְּךָ֙ וַחֲמָ֣תְךָ֔ מֵעִֽירְךָ֥ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם הַר־ קָדְשֶׁ֑ךָ כִּ֤י בַחֲטָאֵ֙ינוּ֙ וּבַעֲוֺנ֣וֹת אֲבֹתֵ֔ינוּ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֧ם וְעַמְּךָ֛ לְחֶרְפָּ֖ה לְכָל־ סְבִיבֹתֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: So now, our God, hear the prayers and petitions of Your servant. For Your sake, O Lord, cause Your face to shine upon Your desolate sanctuary.
passages.sermon:
God is the Lord of Israel.
God listens to His people.
Now, God, please hear the prayer of Your servant.
Please listen to my petitions.
Your sanctuary is desolate.
For Your sake, Lord, let Your face shine on Your sanctuary.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֣ה׀ שְׁמַ֣ע אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ אֶל־ תְּפִלַּ֤ת עַבְדְּךָ֙ וְאֶל־ תַּ֣חֲנוּנָ֔יו וְהָאֵ֣ר פָּנֶ֔יךָ עַל־ מִקְדָּשְׁךָ֖ הַשָּׁמֵ֑ם לְמַ֖עַן אֲדֹנָֽי׃

passages.text: Incline Your ear, O my God, and hear; open Your eyes and see the desolation of the city that bears Your name. For we are not presenting our petitions before You because of our righteous acts, but because of Your great compassion.
passages.sermon:
God, You are my God.
Please listen to me.
Turn Your ear toward me.
Hear my words.
Open Your eyes.
See our desolation.
See the city that carries Your name.
This city is Jerusalem.
We do not bring our requests to You because we are righteous.
We do not come because of our good deeds.
We come because You are very merciful.
We depend on Your great compassion.
passages.original: הַטֵּ֨ה אֱלֹהַ֥י׀ אָזְנְךָ֮ וּֽשֲׁמָע֒ פִּקְחָה עֵינֶ֗יךָ וּרְאֵה֙ שֹֽׁמְמֹתֵ֔ינוּ וְהָעִ֕יר אֲשֶׁר־ נִקְרָ֥א שִׁמְךָ֖ עָלֶ֑יהָ כִּ֣י׀ לֹ֣א עַל־ צִדְקֹתֵ֗ינוּ אֲנַ֨חְנוּ מַפִּילִ֤ים תַּחֲנוּנֵ֙ינוּ֙ לְפָנֶ֔יךָ כִּ֖י עַל־ רַחֲמֶ֥יךָ הָרַבִּֽים׃

passages.text: O Lord, listen! O Lord, forgive! O Lord, hear and act! For Your sake, O my God, do not delay, because Your city and Your people bear Your name.”
passages.sermon:
Daniel prayed to God.
Daniel asked God to listen.
Daniel asked God to forgive.
Daniel asked God to pay attention and act.
Daniel asked God not to delay.
Daniel said, “Do this for Your sake, my God.”
Daniel said, “Your city bears Your name.”
Daniel said, “Your people bear Your name.”
passages.original: אֲדֹנָ֤י׀ שְׁמָ֙עָה֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י׀ סְלָ֔חָה אֲדֹנָ֛י הַֽקֲשִׁ֥יבָה וַעֲשֵׂ֖ה אַל־ תְּאַחַ֑ר לְמַֽעֲנְךָ֣ אֱלֹהַ֔י כִּֽי־ שִׁמְךָ֣ נִקְרָ֔א עַל־ עִירְךָ֖ וְעַל־ עַמֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: While I was speaking, praying, confessing my sin and that of my people Israel, and presenting my petition before the LORD my God concerning His holy mountain— while I was still praying, Gabriel, the man I had seen in the earlier vision, came to me in swift flight about the time of the evening sacrifice.
passages.sermon:
Daniel was a prophet of Israel.
Daniel spoke to God.
Daniel prayed to God.
Daniel confessed his own sin.
Daniel confessed the sin of the people of Israel.
Daniel presented his petition before the LORD his God.
Daniel prayed about God's holy mountain.
Daniel was still speaking in prayer.
Gabriel appeared to Daniel.
Gabriel was the man Daniel had seen in an earlier vision.
Gabriel came to Daniel quickly.
Gabriel reached Daniel at the time of the evening sacrifice.
passages.original: וְע֨וֹד אֲנִ֤י מְדַבֵּר֙ וּמִתְפַּלֵּ֔ל וּמִתְוַדֶּה֙ חַטָּאתִ֔י וְחַטַּ֖את עַמִּ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּמַפִּ֣יל תְּחִנָּתִ֗י לִפְנֵי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהַ֔י עַ֖ל הַר־ קֹ֥דֶשׁ אֱלֹהָֽי׃ וְע֛וֹד אֲנִ֥י מְדַבֵּ֖ר בַּתְּפִלָּ֑ה וְהָאִ֣ישׁ גַּבְרִיאֵ֡ל אֲשֶׁר֩ רָאִ֨יתִי בֶחָז֤וֹן בַּתְּחִלָּה֙ מֻעָ֣ף בִּיעָ֔ף נֹגֵ֣עַ אֵלַ֔י כְּעֵ֖ת מִנְחַת־ עָֽרֶב׃

passages.text: He instructed me and spoke with me, saying: “O Daniel, I have come now to give you insight and understanding.
passages.sermon:
Gabriel is an angel.
Gabriel came to Daniel.
Gabriel spoke to Daniel.
Gabriel said, “Daniel, I have come now.
I have come to give you insight.
I have come to give you understanding.”
passages.original: וַיָּ֖בֶן וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר עִמִּ֑י וַיֹּאמַ֕ר דָּנִיֵּ֕אל עַתָּ֥ה יָצָ֖אתִי לְהַשְׂכִּילְךָ֥ בִינָֽה׃

passages.text: At the beginning of your petitions, an answer went out, and I have come to tell you, for you are highly precious. So consider the message and understand the vision: Seventy weeks are decreed for your people and your holy city to stop their transgression, to put an end to sin, to make atonement for iniquity, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal up vision and prophecy, and to anoint the Most Holy Place.
passages.sermon:
Gabriel is an angel.
Gabriel spoke to Daniel.
Gabriel said he came with a message from God.
God sent an answer when Daniel began to pray.
Gabriel said Daniel is highly precious to God.
Gabriel told Daniel to pay attention to the message.
Gabriel told Daniel to understand the vision.
God has set seventy weeks for Daniel’s people and for the holy city Jerusalem.
God will use this time to stop transgression.
God will use this time to put an end to sin.
God will use this time to make atonement for iniquity.
God will use this time to bring in everlasting righteousness.
God will use this time to seal up vision and prophecy.
God will use this time to anoint the Most Holy Place.
passages.original: בִּתְחִלַּ֨ת תַּחֲנוּנֶ֜יךָ יָצָ֣א דָבָ֗ר וַאֲנִי֙ בָּ֣אתִי לְהַגִּ֔יד כִּ֥י חֲמוּד֖וֹת אָ֑תָּה וּבִין֙ בַּדָּבָ֔ר וְהָבֵ֖ן בַּמַּרְאֶֽה׃ שָׁבֻעִ֨ים שִׁבְעִ֜ים נֶחְתַּ֥ךְ עַֽל־ עַמְּךָ֣׀ וְעַל־ עִ֣יר קָדְשֶׁ֗ךָ לְכַלֵּ֨א הַפֶּ֜שַׁע וּלַחְתֹּם חַטָּאוֹת וּלְכַפֵּ֣ר עָוֺ֔ן וּלְהָבִ֖יא צֶ֣דֶק עֹֽלָמִ֑ים וְלַחְתֹּם֙ חָז֣וֹן וְנָבִ֔יא וְלִמְשֹׁ֖חַ קֹ֥דֶשׁ קָֽדָשִֽׁים׃

passages.text: Know and understand this: From the issuance of the decree to restore and rebuild Jerusalem, until the Messiah, the Prince, there will be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks. It will be rebuilt with streets and a trench, but in times of distress.
passages.sermon:
Daniel was a prophet in exile.
God sent an angel to speak to Daniel.
The angel gave Daniel a message from God.
The angel said, “Know and understand this.”
A command will go out to restore and rebuild Jerusalem.
This command will begin a period of time.
From the command until the coming of the Messiah, the Prince, there will be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks.
Jerusalem will be rebuilt during this time.
The city will have streets and a trench.
The rebuilding will happen in times of trouble.
passages.original: וְתֵדַ֨ע וְתַשְׂכֵּ֜ל מִן־ מֹצָ֣א דָבָ֗ר לְהָשִׁיב֙ וְלִבְנ֤וֹת יְרֽוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ עַד־ מָשִׁ֣יחַ נָגִ֔יד שָׁבֻעִ֖ים שִׁבְעָ֑ה וְשָׁבֻעִ֞ים שִׁשִּׁ֣ים וּשְׁנַ֗יִם תָּשׁוּב֙ וְנִבְנְתָה֙ רְח֣וֹב וְחָר֔וּץ וּבְצ֖וֹק הָעִתִּֽים׃

passages.text: Then after the sixty-two weeks the Messiah will be cut off and will have nothing. Then the people of the prince who is to come will destroy the city and the sanctuary. The end will come like a flood, and until the end there will be war; desolations have been decreed.
passages.sermon:
Daniel was a prophet.
God gave Daniel a vision.
The vision spoke about the future of God’s people and Jerusalem.
After sixty-two weeks, the Messiah will be cut off.
The Messiah will have nothing.
A prince will come in the future.
The people of this prince will destroy the city.
They will destroy the sanctuary.
The end will come quickly, like a flood.
War will continue until the end.
Desolations have been decreed.
passages.original: וְאַחֲרֵ֤י הַשָּׁבֻעִים֙ שִׁשִּׁ֣ים וּשְׁנַ֔יִם יִכָּרֵ֥ת מָשִׁ֖יחַ וְאֵ֣ין ל֑וֹ וְהָעִ֨יר וְהַקֹּ֜דֶשׁ יַ֠שְׁחִית עַ֣ם נָגִ֤יד הַבָּא֙ וְקִצּ֣וֹ בַשֶּׁ֔טֶף וְעַד֙ קֵ֣ץ מִלְחָמָ֔ה נֶחֱרֶ֖צֶת שֹׁמֵמֽוֹת׃

passages.text: And he will confirm a covenant with many for one week, but in the middle of the week he will put an end to sacrifice and offering. And on the wing of the temple will come the abomination that causes desolation, until the decreed destruction is poured out upon him.”
passages.sermon:
A ruler will make a strong covenant with many people for one week.
In the middle of that week, he will stop sacrifice and offering.
An abomination that causes desolation will appear on the wing of the temple.
This will continue until the end that is decreed is poured out on the desolator.
passages.original: וְהִגְבִּ֥יר בְּרִ֛ית לָרַבִּ֖ים שָׁב֣וּעַ אֶחָ֑ד וַחֲצִ֨י הַשָּׁב֜וּעַ יַשְׁבִּ֣ית׀ זֶ֣בַח וּמִנְחָ֗ה וְעַ֨ל כְּנַ֤ף שִׁקּוּצִים֙ מְשֹׁמֵ֔ם וְעַד־ כָּלָה֙ וְנֶ֣חֱרָצָ֔ה תִּתַּ֖ךְ עַל־ שֹׁמֵֽם׃פ
